```shiploop-state
{
  "evidence_refs": [
    "original request, sentences S1-S2 (the only user-supplied source)",
    "exercise brief: repository empty, no tools or files, unattended run",
    "stage guidance 1-8 and Done-when list for the intake stage"
  ],
  "headline": "Intake maps S1-S2 to a local, server-authoritative single-player Battleship game with tests. 7 open questions have recorded defaults and none blocks the run. The game becomes playable only after the run returns and the user starts the server locally.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "summary": "LEGEND: [F] = fact from the request or brief. [A] = assumption recorded as the unattended default. This is not a continuation of an earlier run: [F] the repository is empty and there is no prior run, so Prior-run/recovery guidance does not apply.
OUTCOMES
S1 (what): [F] one small single-player Battleship game, human vs computer. [A] 'small' means one mode, one board size, one opponent, and no accounts, multiplayer, leaderboard, persistence, sound or animation beyond the minimum, with classic rules (OQ1).
S1 (where played): [F] in the browser. [A] a single web page served by the Node server, with no build step, no player install, no CDN or third-party assets, targeting current evergreen desktop browsers with a responsive layout that also works on a phone.
S1 (who and against whom): [F] the requester ('I') is the only human actor. [F] the opponent is the computer. [A] the computer is a server-side module that plays fairly: it sees only the results of its shots, never the player's fleet layout.
S2 (server): [F] Node.js is the server runtime, which is a constraint. [A] the server serves the page and is authoritative for game state and the computer's moves, over a small JSON-over-HTTP API. No WebSockets, because the game is turn-based and single-player. [A] npm, current LTS Node, minimal or zero third-party dependencies (OQ5).
S2 (tests): [F] tests are part of the deliverable and live in the repository. [A] one command, 'npm test', runs them. They cover rules (placement, shot resolution, sinking, win/loss), computer-move legality (never repeats a shot, always terminates) using an injectable seeded RNG for determinism, and HTTP-level server tests, including that unrevealed computer ship positions are not sent to the client before game end.
BOUNDARIES
Repository and run scope: [F] greenfield, empty repository, so there are no conventions, AGENTS.md, CI or lint config to follow. [A] one package at the repository root. [F] the run is isolated and the source checkout stays at its snapshot until the final return.
User constraints: [F] Node.js server, browser play, single-player vs computer, tests included, small. Nothing else was specified and nothing is added here.
Authority limits: [A] the request grants building the game and making it locally runnable. It names no deploy, hosting or publishing target, so deployment, publishing, pushing to a remote, domains and paid services are not granted. [A] the server binds loopback only, with a configurable PORT, makes no outbound network calls at runtime, and nothing is installed globally.
Consumers and entry points: [F] one consumer, the requester, via a browser. [A] entry points are 'npm start' (http://localhost:<port>/) and 'npm test'. The JSON API is consumed only by the page.
Risks: [A] nobody can playtest during the unattended run, so UI quality is verified only by automated tests. [A] game logic or fleet data in client JS would let the player cheat via devtools (mitigated by server authority). [A] unbounded in-memory games could leak memory (mitigated by idle expiry). [A] the computer must never loop or repeat a shot. [A] scope creep toward multiplayer, accounts or deployment is out of scope.
WHERE AND WHEN THE OUTCOME IS VISIBLE
Target: [A] the requester's own machine, as a Node server started from the delivered repository and played at http://localhost:<port>/ in a browser. The request names no other target and no release is needed. [A] no hosted instance will exist, and a deployed outcome would only exist after a release that is not requested. Timing: source and tests exist only in the run's isolated checkout until the final return. The test results are visible earlier, in the verify stage evidence. The game is playable only after the final return, when the requester runs 'npm start' and opens the URL. Playing it is the only person-only step and it blocks nothing in the run.
INTERACTION AND STATE (answered from the request, else default and what it rules out)
Actors and identity: [F] one human plus the computer. [A] no login. The server issues an unguessable game id on 'new game', and the page keeps it in sessionStorage. Rules out accounts and cross-device identity.
Shared state: [F] single-player, so none is shared between people or devices. [A] a second tab is a separate game. Rules out spectators, shared links, multiplayer and leaderboards.
Lifetime: [A] game state is held in server memory keyed by game id. It ends on win or loss, on 'new game', on idle expiry, or on server restart. A page reload during a live game resumes it via the stored id. Rules out a database, history and stats.
Hidden information: [A] the computer's fleet is hidden from the player until game end. The server returns only per-shot results (miss, hit, sunk with ship name) and reveals the full fleet at game over. The player's fleet is visible to the player and never used by the computer to aim. Rules out client-side fleet storage.
What the runtime provides: [A] Node gives http, in-process memory, crypto.randomUUID and node:test. The browser gives the DOM, fetch and sessionStorage. Neither provides identity, game state or persistence, so the build supplies a minimal session map itself.
OPEN QUESTIONS (owner; blocks; what discovery must establish first)
OQ1 Rules variant: owner is a recorded default, since no rules source exists. Blocks the engine design and the expected values in tests. Discovery must first confirm no house-rules doc or prior game exists in the workspace. Default: classic 10x10, fleet carrier 5, battleship 4, cruiser 3, submarine 3, destroyer 2, one shot per turn, no extra turn on a hit, player moves first, a sinking is announced. Rules out Salvo and other variants.
OQ2 Ship placement: owner is a recorded default. Blocks the setup UI and the API shape. Discovery needs to find no stated preference. Default: both fleets are placed randomly and the player sees their own fleet. Rules out manual or drag-and-drop placement, which is cheap to add later.
OQ3 Computer strength: owner is a recorded default. Blocks the AI module and its tests. Discovery needs to find no difficulty requirement. Default: hunt-and-target (random or parity search, then neighbours after a hit), no cheating, no difficulty selector.
OQ4 Logic location and API: owner is a recorded default. Blocks architecture, the test layering and the client/server split. Discovery has nothing to inspect because the repository is empty. Default: server-authoritative state with a small JSON API (new game, fire, state). Rules out a purely client-side game.
OQ5 Node and tooling: owner is discovery (environment check) with a recorded default. Blocks scaffolding, 'engines' and the test command. Discovery must establish the installed 'node --version' and 'npm --version' in the run environment, and the Node version on the requester's machine if it is knowable. Default: the active LTS, npm, built-in node:test, built-in http, no framework, vanilla HTML/CSS/JS client.
OQ6 Test depth: owner is discovery with a recorded default. Blocks verify-stage design and the definition of done. Discovery must establish whether a headless browser is available in the run environment. Default: logic unit tests, API tests over real HTTP, and a served-page smoke check. No browser end-to-end tests unless a browser is available. Residual risk: actual in-browser behaviour is unverified.
OQ7 UI details (accessibility, mobile, wording): owner is a recorded default. Blocks only front-end polish. Discovery needs no input. Default: a plain responsive page, click or tap to fire, text status messages, hit and miss distinguished by more than colour, and no sound.
DISCOVERY SOURCE HINTS (leads, not verified facts)
The request names no team, workspace, channel, internal site, owner or private repository. [A] the requester is the only owner and they cannot be asked during the run. Leads: the run environment itself (Node, npm and browser availability), any KNOWLEDGE/ or AGENTS.md present in the run workspace, and the requester's other repositories for a preferred Node style or test runner (unverified). Public references: classic Battleship rules and the Node.js release and LTS schedule. Ambiguous terms to resolve from evidence: 'small', 'against the computer', 'tests' (unit or end-to-end), and 'Node.js for the server' (static host or authoritative server). Any sensitive locator goes only in an authorized private store and none is recorded here."
}
```
